 Blazers Notes: Lillard, Avdija, Henderson, Rotation, Arena
 By Luke Adams |
 at October 21, 2026 12:59 pm 
 As he prepares to play on Wednesday in his first regular season game since March 18, 2025, Trail Blazers point guard Damian Lillard admits he thought about trying to return from his Achilles tear during the 2026 postseason. However, he tells Marc J. Spears of Andscape that he ultimately decided it made more sense to take another offseason to make sure he was 100% and had regained full confidence in that surgically repaired Achilles tendon.
 “The reason I sat out the entire season was because I wanted to check every box,” Lillard said. “I didn’t want to come limping back or having second thoughts about, ‘Man, can I do this? Can I do that? What should I stay away from?’ I checked every box and I cleared every box, so that was my priority in that process, and I did exactly that.” 
 If Lillard’s goal was to make sure he looked and felt like his old self before getting back on the court, then new head coach Micah Nori believes it’s mission accomplished, writes Spears.
 “There’s really no loss of his — I’m not going to say explosiveness, but his quickness,” Nori said. “But the other thing is, like I tell people: He hurt his lower body, not his upper body. He can still shoot the thing, so his game is not reliant on all that quickness. It’s just more of him getting shots and us finding space for him. 
 “And the one difference that you’ll see with Dame now is he’ll be off the ball a little bit more than what he was earlier in his career. We can still play him, obviously, in the pick-and-roll. … He doesn’t have to do all that to be able to find him open shots more so in the flow. And you see him competing at the defensive end as well.” 
 Here’s more on the Trail Blazers:
 Within an interesting story about 2012 Blazers lottery pick Meyers Leonard , who was selected five spots after Lillard and will be in Portland on Wednesday to see his former teammate make his Blazers return, Jason Quick of The Athletic quotes Lillard as saying he “should have never left” Portland. “I never saw (being traded elsewhere as) being part of my story,” said the veteran guard, who requested a change of scenery in 2023 due to frustrations with the Blazers’ direction. “The fact that it worked out how it did — I’m back here, with a really good team, and I’m healthy — it just feels right.” 
 Star forward Deni Avdija was a surprise inclusion on the Trail Blazers’ first injury report of the season, writes Joe Freeman of The Oregonian . Avdija is listed as questionable to play on Wednesday vs. Phoenix due to right ankle soreness.
 After not reaching an agreement on a rookie scale extension with the Blazers prior to Monday’s deadline, Scoot Henderson – the third overall pick in the 2023 draft – enters his fourth NBA season with more to prove than ever, writes Sean Highkin for The Rose Garden Report (Substack link). For what it’s worth, Henderson has received rave reviews in recent weeks, with Jrue Holiday calling him the MVP of camp and Nori comparing him to prime Russell Westbrook , Highkin notes. “There would be nothing happier for me than if next year we had to pay Scoot a ton of money to keep him,” Nori said. “He knows that he’s an NBA player. He knows he’s going to get another contract. We just hope it’s with the Portland Trail Blazers.” 
 Nori has said he intends to use a 10-man rotation, according to Quick , who suggests that Lillard, Ja Morant , Toumani Camara , Avdija, and Donovan Clingan will be the usual starters, with Holiday, Robert Williams , and Henderson as the top reserves. The ninth man will likely be forward Sidy Cissoko , Quick continues, with Vit Krejci , Micah Potter , and Branden Carlson battling for regular minutes.
 Bill Oram of The Oregonian (subscription required) shares the latest developments in the Moda Center negotiations between the Blazers and the city of Portland, suggesting that language in the Trail Blazers’ lease requiring the team to keep the arena in “first-class” condition continues to be an issue. According to Oram, Blazers owner Tom Dundon insisted that city officials put a dollar amount on that “first-class” mandate and the number they came back with was “upwards of $1 billion,” which Dundon balked at. At least one meeting between Dundon and city officials is scheduled to take place this week, but it’s unclear whether there will be any others, Oram adds.
